column1: # Mario Kart World (Switch 2): two builds of the same game, both registered and treated alike: 1.0.0 (the dump supplied on the Android development machine: SDK 19.3.3, main 9e244438..., no
# separate update, no control data) and 1.8.0 (SDK 21.4.0: main d00e4f39..., subsdk0 = NintendoSDK movie 746302f4..., subsdk1 = nn::ecli 8dec9c0b..., sdk 7a68b13d...). Nothing in this
# profile or in the host is keyed to one of them: the shader tables are the union of both (shader_optional.tsv: the keys only one build has), and a dump takes the modules of the build
# row it matches (pack_android.py). In bring-up on Android: Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive, Havok 2023.2), built for the Switch 2 (spec Ounce), NVN2; modules main + subsdk0
# + sdk, and for 1.8.0 subsdk1 too (1.0.0 has one module less: its subsdk0 is the ecli, whose allocator main imports).
# Packed from a dump folder (base/). Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code), as Donkey Kong Bananza.
# One row a version number: the 1.0.0 dump is version 0 (the base game); 1.8.0 is update 524288 (a dump that keeps its code under another number, in base/ as the first 1.8.0 dump did,
# is that build all the same: the launcher and the packer compare build IDs, not version numbers). Display versions as the game's releases are named
# every module of either build, in load order: a dump takes those of its own build (a module the other build has and this one lacks is left out)
# Line 4 of System/RegionLangMask.txt is the build ID of the main its RomFS was made for (1.8.0: line 3 "180", line 4 d00e4f39...), as in Donkey Kong Bananza: a dump whose
# RomFS is another build's data under 1.8.0's code (GitHub #27 / #44: CRASH sig=11 at main+0x8bfc0 1.7 s in) is refused at Add / Prepare and on the card
# The NPDM declares 64 MB of system resource (virtual address memory on; 1.8.0's NPDM differs only by the services chat:u, mnpp:app and stpl:u). nninitStartup sets the heap to the
# free application memory less a fixed reserve (main+0x84790: 0x5dc00000 in 1.8.0, 0x60400000 in the earlier base build, whose Mac heap check measured 0x1dbc00000): 0x1de400000
# (7.47 GB) in 1.8.0, by that formula (not measured), within the 7.75 GB heap region.
# The alias region holds the SDK's AddressRegionManager node area (0x3fe00000) and then the regions the game maps physical memory into (earlier base build: main+0x68524c), past +1.6 GB within 8 s
# of boot (DM_REGIONS, Switch-sized DM_ALIAS_SIZE); with a 1 GB alias region the first ones got no address and the game read a null object (main+0xc10170). 4 GB: the node area
# and the 1.57 GB (1.53 GB in 1.8.0) the 9 GB pool leaves beside the heap, with room for fragmentation. The Switch 2's 9 GB pool (as Donkey Kong Bananza; not measured)
# agl's render buffer binding: Donkey Kong Bananza's clears are wrapped in render conditions; the same engine, not yet checked on this game
# The 3D scenes' size follows the operation mode and the Switch 2 graphics scale, not the window (README, Render resolution): the Android launcher's Game resolution
# sets these instead of DM_WINDOW_SIZE. <choice> <DM_GRAPHICS_SCALE> <operation mode>: handheld scale 0 crops 1920x1080, handheld scale 2 1280x720 (phone rH0 / rH2);
# Original has no row: the game's own (console, scale 1: 2048x1152)
